instruction: Find Team Fortress 2 and add the Team Fortress 2 Soundtrack to your shopping cart.

metadata.explanation: Task variation: User needs to find Team Fortress 2 game and add the soundtrack DLC to cart. Evaluator checks cart page content for 'Team Fortress 2 Soundtrack'. Similar pattern to original Dota 2 task but with different game and specific DLC item. Reuses existing Chrome evaluation infrastructure.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses get_page_info getter to retrieve Steam cart page HTML content
Metric function is_added_to_steam_cart correctly accesses rule['items'] directly (proper parameter handling for type='rule')
Verification logic semantically matches instruction: checks if 'Team Fortress 2 Soundtrack' is present in cart page content
Expected value 'Team Fortress 2 Soundtrack' correctly matches the item specified in the instruction
Evaluator verifies the final outcome (item added to cart) which is the core requirement of the instruction
Substring matching in HTML content is fragile - may fail if Steam uses different formatting, capitalization, or special characters (e.g., 'Team Fortress® 2 Soundtrack', 'TF2 Soundtrack')
Evaluator only checks final state (item in cart), does not verify the 'Locate Team Fortress 2' intermediate step, though this is acceptable as it focuses on end result
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using more robust HTML parsing (BeautifulSoup) to extract cart item names instead of raw substring matching on HTML content
Could use case-insensitive matching or fuzzy string matching to handle minor variations in item naming
Consider extracting structured data from cart page (e.g., item titles in specific HTML elements) rather than searching entire page content
